main.title: Beijing 2008 Olympic Games
main.summary: Beijing hosted the Olympic Games from 8 to 24 August 2008, the first edition held in China.

cards.heading: Beijing 2008 Olympic Games
cards.text: Beijing hosted the Olympic Games from 8 to 24 August 2008, the first edition held in China. A total of 10,942 athletes from 204 National Olympic Committees competed across 28 sports and 302 events. The scale brought national teams from around the world to the Chinese capital for more than two weeks of competition. Beijing followed Tokyo in 1964 and Seoul in 1988 as the third East Asian host of the Summer Games. The event established Beijing 2008 as a major moment in China's history of hosting international sport.

main.title: The Dark Knight
main.summary: The Dark Knight returned to Gotham City in 2008, with Batman, James Gordon and district attorney Harvey Dent working against organised crime.

cards.heading: The Dark Knight
cards.text: The Dark Knight returned to Gotham City in 2008, with Batman, James Gordon and district attorney Harvey Dent working against organised crime. The Joker disrupts their alliance by pushing the city towards chaos and testing the limits of Batman's methods. Christopher Nolan directed and co-wrote the screenplay with Jonathan Nolan, drawing on Batman comics and crime dramas. Christian Bale plays Batman opposite Heath Ledger's Joker and Aaron Eckhart's Dent. Dent's position between the two rivals gives the conflict its central human story, continuing the heightened realism established in Batman Begins.

main.title: Breaking Bad
main.subtitle: A chemistry teacher turns expertise into a criminal business
main.summary: Vince Gilligan's Breaking Bad follows Walter White, an Albuquerque chemistry teacher who begins manufacturing methamphetamine after a cancer diagnosis. Bryan Cranston plays Walter, with Aaron Paul as former pupil and partner Jesse Pinkman. The series premiered on AMC in the United States on 20 January 2008, beginning a story in which a proposed solution to a family crisis becomes an expanding source of harm.

cards.heading: A solution with consequences
cards.text: Vince Gilligan's Breaking Bad follows Walter White, an Albuquerque chemistry teacher who begins manufacturing methamphetamine after a cancer diagnosis. Bryan Cranston plays Walter, with Aaron Paul as former pupil and partner Jesse Pinkman. The series premiered on AMC in the United States on 20 January 2008, beginning a story in which a proposed solution to a family crisis becomes an expanding source of harm.

cards.heading: A partnership under pressure
cards.text: Walter's scientific knowledge gives him an advantage, but running the business requires decisions that expertise cannot make for him. Jesse brings a different experience of the people involved, and their partnership repeatedly shifts between dependence, affection and exploitation. Each attempt to control a problem creates obligations elsewhere. The continuing story makes earlier choices difficult to escape: an arrangement that once looked temporary becomes something the characters must protect, explain or destroy.

cards.heading: The ingenuity of a dangerous plan
cards.text: The series often lets a plan unfold through objects and actions before explaining its full purpose. Laboratories, vehicles and domestic spaces become working parts of those plans, while the desert offers a very different sense of exposure. Gilligan's approach keeps suspense close to character: Walter's ingenuity can be impressive at the same moment that its use becomes alarming. Cranston's changing performance follows that tension, allowing pride and resentment to emerge beneath the explanations Walter gives for his conduct.

main.title: Large Hadron Collider
main.summary: The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is the world's largest and highest-energy particle accelerator.

cards.heading: Large Hadron Collider
cards.text:
The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is the world's largest and highest-energy particle accelerator. It was built by the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN) between 1998 and 2008, in collaboration with over 10,000 scientists, and hundreds of universities and laboratories across more than 100 countries. It lies in a tunnel 27 kilometres (17 mi) in circumference and as deep as 175 metres (574 ft) beneath the France–Switzerland border near Geneva.

The first collisions were achieved in 2010 at an energy of 3.5 tera-electronvolts (TeV) per beam, about four times the previous world record. The discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC was announced in 2012. Between 2013 and 2015, the LHC was shut down and upgraded; after those upgrades it reached 6.5 TeV per beam (13.0 TeV total collision energy). At the end of 2018, it was shut down for maintenance and further upgrades, and reopened over three years later in April 2022.

main.title: Bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers
main.summary: Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy on 15 September 2008 after negotiations to rescue the investment bank failed.

cards.heading: Bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers
cards.text: Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy on 15 September 2008 after negotiations to rescue the investment bank failed. Heavy exposure to subprime mortgages had undermined its position, with a credit downgrade approaching. The filing involved more than 600 billion dollars in assets and became the largest in American history. It deepened the financial crisis: stock markets fell, investors withdrew money from funds and banks grew more reluctant to lend to each other. The government and Federal Reserve introduced emergency measures as the failure spread fear through an already fragile financial system.

main.title: United States presidential election
main.summary: Barack Obama won the United States presidential election on 4 November 2008, becoming the first African American elected to the office.

cards.heading: United States presidential election
cards.text: Barack Obama won the United States presidential election on 4 November 2008, becoming the first African American elected to the office. Running with Joe Biden, he defeated Republican John McCain and his running mate Sarah Palin. Obama had secured the Democratic nomination after a closely contested primary against Hillary Clinton. McCain had emerged from the Republican race earlier that year. With George W. Bush barred from a third term, the election brought a new administration to the White House and marked a historic change in who could hold the presidency.

main.title: Slumdog Millionaire
main.subtitle: A quiz-show contestant explains the life behind his answers
main.summary: Slumdog Millionaire follows Jamal Malik, an eighteen-year-old from Mumbai who reaches the final stages of a television quiz show. His success leads to an accusation of cheating, and the explanation unfolds through memories of his life. Directed by Danny Boyle, with Loveleen Tandan as co-director in India, the film opened in the United States on 12 November 2008.

cards.heading: The life behind the answers
cards.text: Slumdog Millionaire follows Jamal Malik, an eighteen-year-old from Mumbai who reaches the final stages of a television quiz show. His success leads to an accusation of cheating, and the explanation unfolds through memories of his life. Directed by Danny Boyle, with Loveleen Tandan as co-director in India, the film opened in the United States on 12 November 2008.

cards.heading: A broadcast with a personal purpose
cards.text: Each question leads back to an encounter that gave Jamal a particular piece of knowledge. The structure links the television studio to his childhood with his brother Salim, their journeys and his continuing search for Latika. Answers that appear improbable to the show's viewers become understandable within those experiences. The parallel story also changes the stakes of the broadcast: Jamal's reason for appearing is tied to a person he hopes will be watching, rather than simply the money on offer.

cards.heading: Connecting the episodes
cards.text: Simon Beaufoy's screenplay, adapted from Vikas Swarup's Q&A, gives the story its framework of questions and recollections. A.R. Rahman's score connects its rapidly changing locations with recurring melodies and energetic rhythms. Dev Patel and Freida Pinto play the adult Jamal and Latika, while younger performers carry the earlier episodes. The film won eight Academy Awards, including best picture and direction, taking its mixture of romance, suspense and television spectacle to a wide international audience.

main.title: Swine flu pandemic
main.summary: A new H1N1 influenza strain spread internationally in 2009, leading the World Health Organization to declare a pandemic that lasted from June 2009 to August 2010.

cards.heading: Swine flu pandemic
cards.text: A new H1N1 influenza strain spread internationally in 2009, leading the World Health Organization to declare a pandemic that lasted from June 2009 to August 2010. The first identified human case was in La Gloria, Mexico. The virus combined genetic material associated with bird, swine and human influenza, giving rise to the name swine flu. Its pattern differed from many seasonal strains because older adults were less disproportionately affected. A small proportion of patients, including previously healthy people, developed serious respiratory complications. The outbreak brought a new influenza strain into worldwide public-health attention.

main.title: Avatar
main.summary: James Cameron's Avatar appeared in 2009, setting its story on Pandora, a moon threatened by human mining.

cards.heading: Avatar
cards.text: James Cameron's Avatar appeared in 2009, setting its story on Pandora, a moon threatened by human mining. People operate genetically engineered Na'vi bodies remotely, using these avatars to interact with the indigenous population. The expansion of the colony places a local Na'vi community's existence at risk. Cameron had written an early treatment in 1994 and originally planned a release after Titanic, but delayed production because he believed the available technology could not yet realise the film. The finished science-fiction story brought that long-developed world to the screen.

main.title: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
main.subtitle: Dumbledore prepares Harry through memories of Voldemort
main.summary: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince follows Harry as Dumbledore begins preparing him for the confrontation ahead. Memories of Voldemort's youth provide clues, and the return of former teacher Horace Slughorn offers a way to reach information that has been withheld. David Yates directs again, with Jim Broadbent as Slughorn and Steve Kloves returning as screenwriter. The sixth film opened on 15 July 2009. Harry's investigation runs beside a second mystery: the handwritten advice in a Potions textbook once owned by someone calling himself the Half-Blood Prince.

cards.heading: A history with practical consequences
cards.text: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince follows Harry as Dumbledore begins preparing him for the confrontation ahead. Memories of Voldemort's youth provide clues, and the return of former teacher Horace Slughorn offers a way to reach information that has been withheld. David Yates directs again, with Jim Broadbent as Slughorn and Steve Kloves returning as screenwriter. The sixth film opened on 15 July 2009. Harry's investigation runs beside a second mystery: the handwritten advice in a Potions textbook once owned by someone calling himself the Half-Blood Prince.

cards.heading: School life under a gathering threat
cards.text: The film repeatedly places ordinary adolescent uncertainty beside the advancing conflict. Ron's relationship with Lavender and Hermione's response occupy the same corridors as Draco Malfoy's secret work, while Harry moves between his feelings for Ginny and his suspicions about what is happening inside the castle. Cinematographer Bruno Delbonnel gives these spaces a subdued, often shadowed appearance. Nicholas Hooper's score includes delicate passages as well as more threatening writing, allowing private conversations and Dumbledore's investigation to share a school year whose familiar routines are becoming increasingly difficult to sustain.
